items.headline: Frost Advisory issued September 2 at 12:12PM AKDT until September 3 at 8:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures as low as 32 will result in frost formation.

* WHERE...City and Borough of Yakutat.

* WHEN...From 2 AM to 8 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Frost could harm sensitive outdoor vegetation. Sensitive
outdoor plants may be killed if left uncovered.
items.instruction:
Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. Sensitive
plants and shrubs should be covered or brought indoors if possible.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 5:44AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A strong front moves toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight
tonight. Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled
with a lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2
feet above normal high tide late tonight into early Thursday
morning. Strongest winds are expected to peak Thursday morning,
with up to 0.5 inches of rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are
perpendicular to the southerly wind direction, such as
Kwigillingok, have a higher chance of seeing impacts with this
f
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 5:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move in Wednesday afternoon into Wednesday evening, with
moderate to heavy rain and gusty winds expected through
Thursday. Rainfall totals are expected to be around 1 to 1.50
inches, with wind gusts up to 55 mph out of the east/southeast.

* WHERE...St. Lawrence Island.

* WHEN...Wednesday September 2 through Thursday September 3.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain and gusty winds could make travel difficult
at times.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 5:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move into Western Alaska Wednesday into Thursday, with
widespread rain and gusty winds expected. Water levels late
Thursday through Saturday morning could rise 2 to 4 feet above
the normal high tide line in the Norton Sound, and 1 to 2 feet
above the normal high tide line along the Yukon Delta Coast.
